headline: Dalrymple Bay Infrastructure exits buy list after 40% gain as market discovers its uniquely secure cash flows
reasoning: Dalrymple Bay operates the world's largest met coal terminal and was recommended when it yielded approximately 6%, with the view that its cash flows were among the most secure on the ASX. The business has 11 customers paying cross-collateralised, take-or-pay access charges, meaning if one customer cannot pay, the remaining ten must cover the shortfall. All operating costs are pass-throughs to customers under contract, eliminating most expense risk. The company has also been quietly upgrading facilities, which under its contractual structure allows it to grow its asset base and lift access charges over time. Distributions have grown a little faster than forecast, drawing significant market attention, brokerage coverage and fund ownership, which drove the 40% price rise and pushed the stock off the buy list.
quote: Yeah, look, I I think this is just a case of the market suddenly discovering a business that was previously just being ignored. Um because nothing has really changed about this company except the amount of attention and the and the price has gone up a long way. And it's funny because when we recommended this stock, it was generally to, I would say, um mute enthusiasm. I think you and I bought it, John. Um I was very worried about where markets were. So, I actually made it quite a large position, but expected... the expectation was that this this was actually a very simple, boring business where nothing had changed since the company had listed. And um and and the valuation looked very cheap, but the um uh the yield when we recommended it, I think it was uh about 6%. And when you look at what the business actually does, um you kind of realize how attractive those sort of returns are for the amount of risk you're holding because um we've called this probably the most secure cash flows on the ASX.
